# Paired default-off compatibility evidence for issue 113

This source runner compares a repaired existing-language compiler with the issue-113 compiler on the **same original inputs**. It is a measurement workflow, not a claim that the old suite or reference standard library is verified. Raw failures, warnings, resource ceilings, timeouts and missing jobs remain visible.

The default workflow has 54 matched-pair jobs and four compiler builds. It preserves the original canonical matrices: development suite with the AdditionalAxioms option absent; shipped suite with its existing option off and on; and both lines' seven Std parts under Z3 5.1.0 and the canonical reference solver, including both shipped axiom settings. Optional global refresh coverage and six Unicode-setting controls per line are separately labelled; selecting both adds 16 jobs. They never replace an original denominator.

`spec.json` pins the public original revisions, audited ordered source recipes, resulting complete/Core/Driver tree identities, final revisions and solver archives. The repaired sources are reconstructed by applying the included patches to clean public originals; private commits are not needed to build them. Composition refuses a dirty/wrong checkout, an altered patch, a path outside each explicitly audited patch scope, or a mismatched resulting tree. The existing Core-only recipe remains unchanged for the shipped line. Development applies that unchanged Core patch first and the separately reviewed three-line #104 `RunCommand.cs` patch second; no other Driver or source path is permitted. Its full tree is `cc3a0308365b83ac34932674dede0270fd6fdb44`, its Core tree remains `e2e8bb392aa2d2b02650370f0bbc66ac82107ff5`, and its Driver tree is `923d23afbe9c3965c87014c7aefbc8c64abb7ccf`, matching the final development Driver tree. The source patches include the separately reviewed repairs for 132, 141, 142, 143, 145, 146 and 148. The development allocation port retains the existing shipped owner substitution of actual type arguments in a revealed constant-field RHS; the same one-hunk correction is shared with the final development compiler. The #104 repair makes the existing run command honor the build-output alias before compilation; it has no Core change. The combined recipes do not import issue-113 operation views or feature admission. Each source composition receipt lists every applied patch, hash, exact changed path and computed full/Core/Driver tree.

The old canonical helpers, workflow and expected tables are copied unchanged in `canonical/<line>`. The plans contain 1,092 development programs and 1,081 shipped programs. Input receipts cover 4,608/4,770 original tracked suite/library files, including committed `.doo` binaries. Before measurement, pure source checks reproduce the plans and validate every byte. Newly added issue-113 fixtures are outside this denominator. Compiler identity includes the actual Core, Driver, main DLL, all other published managed components, deps/runtimeconfig files and apphost; packaged library hashes are retained too. Four original suite cases select the packaged libraries, so their actual bundle assets are part of the recorded toolchain boundary.

## Commands and capacity

Each old canonical default command retains the original helper's exact proof options. The suite's normal settings are resource limit 16,000,000, verification time limit 0, declaration-order normalization 0, one core and allowed warnings, with the helper's original precedence for explicit program settings. Existing exceptions stay explicit: development `SchorrWaite-stages` keeps its 90-second/one-core options; the two old custom resource limits stay; a shipped own Boogie option retains its original selection behavior. No seed, schema or optional proof flag is added.

Both compilers omit `--extended-newtype-bases`, whose final default is false and whose option is absent from the repaired baseline. Development always omits AdditionalAxioms. Shipped axiom-off uses the original wrapper's omission; axiom-on injects `--additional-axioms` before the original options, preserving explicit own-option precedence. The optional refresh cohort injects refresh only if the RUN plan has no explicit setting. Both axes retain explicit false controls. This extra cohort is not an original canonical expected table.

Std keeps the original project files, their resource limits, the committed old `.doo` inputs, the Makefile/helper's sorted target-file lists, four cores and verification time limit 0. Declaration order remains the canonical default. The seven independent parts are sharded by part; their internal source/declaration ordering is unchanged. No suite-style declaration-order override is imposed on Std. Reference solvers remain diagnostic evidence, and their actual failures are not called green. Std resource counts can move under its existing default order; every movement is reported rather than silently tolerated or attributed to the feature.

A baseline/final pair runs sequentially on the same host and input directory, in balanced deterministic order. At most four pairs execute concurrently on one suite runner; Std uses one pair. Each invocation is a fresh compiler process. Original 900-second suite/5,400-second Std process caps, a 240-minute job cap and 12-job workflow concurrency cap bound work. A killed or unfinished pair stays incomplete; completed half-pair artifacts and append-only progress events are retained. The default workload requests 6,508 suite invocations plus 84 Std invocations, counting both compilers. Selecting both extra cohorts requests 13,148 invocations total.

## Observations and interpretation

JSON logging and `--bprint` are appended to the same invocation that performs verification. The modern verifier prints the translated program before obtaining verification tasks; the legacy translation path similarly prints before yielding the same program to verification. JSON logging subscribes to existing results. There is no second full translation/proof gate, `--no-verify`, coverage switch, axiom switch or solver tracing added for observations.

Every arm records the actual argument array, input cwd, compiler/component identity, solver executable hash/version, process exit, stdout/stderr, all warning lines, verdict, per-declaration total resource count, per-batch resource count/outcome/seed and all translated modules' Boogie files. Resource units, rather than elapsed time, measure proof cost. Runtime durations are capacity observations only.

Both raw and normalized Boogie hashes are stored. Normalization is restricted to identified compiler-version comments, the known input/observation roots in comments, and the source root prefix in `captureState` diagnostic attributes. Line/column/state suffixes remain. Unknown version text remains unchanged. Semantic literals, formulas, attributes/IDs, checksums, declaration order, triggers and axioms are retained. Exact normalized whole-program equality therefore establishes that the compared translated programs have no changed background schema. A hash difference requires inspection; it is not discarded as harmless. These are translated Boogie program hashes **before engine VC generation**, not hashes of solver queries or passified VCs.

`run.py aggregate` reports actual denominators, absent jobs, duplicates, incomplete pairs, verdict movements, resource/batch movements, warnings and Boogie movements. Unrequested optional cohorts are distinguished from missing requested evidence by the uploaded workload receipt. Original unrepaired expected-table movements are separate context; they do not automatically attribute a change to an independent repair. Identical failing outcomes establish compatibility observations, not verification of the failed declarations. Missing logs, unresolved programs, crashes and timeouts limit resource/BPL comparability and are reported explicitly. Successful Actions steps alone are not the evidence conclusion.

## Pure preparation

`matrix.py` selects a workload without invoking Dafny; `plan.py --check` regenerates the original source plans; `prepare.py inputs` validates inputs; `prepare.py compose` applies only the audited source patch and checks tree identity; `prepare.py identity` hashes a published bundle without invoking it. Only `run.py run` invokes verification. The workflow builds and measures on standard public CI runners. No local compiler, solver, proof workload or backend build is part of source preparation.

The full default-off workload for these exact compiler pins remains unmeasured until its corresponding public build and measurement artifacts exist. The earlier development Std triad uses `b615831aaa26fea72364627d0fe6040f10e49eee`/`a5304cd9aeb5e4fd12700aa2e61125a904d58996` and remains separate historical evidence. Its inherited proof failures and unresolved resource changes are not waived by the later Driver composition. Before dispatching against a later final product, update `spec.json`'s final pins explicitly; keep the original input plans and repaired patches fixed, and retain the new exact compiler receipts.
